review_findings.description: is_err, is_ok, catch_unwind or should_panic, which accept any failure rather than the failure the case is about
review_findings.rationale: Phase 2 replaced every broad is_err assertion on a wide API with a typed expected-failure assertion carrying a structured rejection reason. What remains is on APIs whose failure set has one member.

review_findings.description: exists, is_file or is_dir, each of which reports an IO failure as absence
review_findings.rationale: Phase 1 migrated every assertion about the filesystem to the test_fs helpers, which use symlink_metadata and fail on an IO error instead of reading it as a missing file. Remaining uses inside test files are setup guards, where absence and failure lead to the same next step.

review_findings.description: to_string_lossy or from_utf8_lossy, which replace unsupported input with a substitute character and then assert on the substitute
review_findings.rationale: Phase 5 removed lossy conversion from every assertion path. Remaining uses are in rendered diagnostic output, where a replacement character is what a reader should see rather than a failure.

review_findings.description: a bound comparison, a negated emptiness check or an any() assertion, each of which passes on more states than the one the case is about
review_findings.rationale: Phase 4 replaced the positive assertions that only proved something existed with exact counts and exact identities. What remains asserts a genuine bound or a genuine existential, where the exact value is not the contract.

review_findings.description: find_map selection, which silently picks one of several matches
review_findings.rationale: Phase 4 gave artifact lookup a typed inventory that rejects a duplicate path instead of returning whichever entry came first.

review_findings.description: an assertion that some output contains a fragment, which passes on any output that happens to include it
review_findings.rationale: The integration suite has zero contains-mode diagnostic contracts after Phase 7. Remaining contains assertions are over rendered prose and over error messages, where the wording a reader sees is the contract and an exact whole-output match would pin unrelated formatting.

review_findings.description: a sleep, a spin loop or a wall-clock reading, each of which can make the result depend on how fast the machine is
review_findings.rationale: Phase 6 replaced every expected transition with a condition variable or a channel. A remaining wall-clock deadline is deadlock protection whose failure names the observed state, not the thing being asserted.

review_findings.description: an assertion over source text read at compile time, which proves what a file says rather than what the code does
review_findings.rationale: Phase 8 moved the tree-wide source bans into the source audit, which reports typed findings and says plainly that source text is not behaviour evidence. Remaining include_str! uses are fixtures and manifests, not claims about behaviour.

review_findings.description: a test item gated to one platform family, which no other platform's lane executes
review_findings.rationale: These own behaviour of a real platform API — symlinks, permission bits, non-UTF-8 filenames — that the other platforms do not have. Phase 8 makes them visible instead of silent by running the Linux, macOS and Windows CI gates, so a platform-owned test is executed somewhere rather than nowhere.

review_findings.description: a hardcoded /tmp literal that no filesystem call on the same line acts on
review_findings.rationale: These are path values handed to pure path logic — rejection rules, prefix comparison, command argument assembly — which never touch the filesystem. A /tmp literal that does reach the filesystem is the hard rule tmp_literal_reaching_the_filesystem, which fails this audit.

review_findings.description: std::env::temp_dir(), which names a directory every process on the machine shares
review_findings.rationale: Used as an existing-directory value for path logic that must not create anything, in tests that assert on the resulting path rather than on disk. An owned workspace comes from tempfile::tempdir.

declared_findings.description: test_support::temp_dir returned uncreated paths; callers had to create_dir_all manually
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: renamed to unused_temp_path with non-existence contract; ALL created-workspace fixtures migrated to tempfile::tempdir() with owned cleanup; remaining 3 uses (validate_dangerous_project, output_defaults, output_overrides) are genuine uncreated-path contracts

declared_findings.description: Hardcoded /tmp/ paths in test files
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: all hardcoded /tmp/ paths removed and replaced with tempfile::tempdir() or unused_temp_path

declared_findings.description: exists()/is_file()/is_dir() mask IO errors as absence
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: test_fs helpers use symlink_metadata; all negative exists() assertions in build_orchestration_tests, build_cleanup_tests, check_tests, and cli_tests migrated to assert_path_missing; fixture discovery uses symlink_metadata with fail-closed on metadata errors

declared_findings.description: Broad is_err()/error_count()>0 assertions accept wrong failure at multi-lane boundaries; String-only transport in integration fixture/expectation/runner forced substring error identity
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: all 26 build_orchestration is_err() assertions migrated to assert_output_rejection; benchmark errors carry typed FrontendBenchmarkFailureKind + diagnostic_codes; fixture/expectation loading returns FixtureLoadError{kind,message} (Filesystem/Manifest/ExpectationParse/ExpectationContract/FixtureContract/PathBoundary); runner returns TestRunnerError with Options/SuitePolicy/InventoryReport/TriageReport/Selection/ThreadPool/Fixture kinds; negative self-tests assert error.kind; compile_project_frontend broad is_err() seeds made exact; containment test uses assert_output_rejection; busy benchmark test uses owned entry + TimingSession kind

declared_findings.description: first_infrastructure_error_for_tests only returned the first infrastructure error
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: infrastructure_errors_for_tests() iterator scans all error diagnostics

declared_findings.description: WarningBuilder created StringId from fresh StringTable; CaseExecutionResult had impossible states
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: WarningBuilder uses active string_table; CaseExecutionResult constructors removed from production; runner tests use panic_if_called; terse_reporting uses valid BuildResult and CompilerMessages in all synthetic fixtures

declared_findings.description: CurrentDirGuard::Drop discarded restoration failures
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: Option<PathBuf> take pattern prevents double-restore; finish() returns Result; Drop panics on restore failure (non-unwinding) or reports to stderr (unwinding); restore-failure injection seam; regression tests for both finish-error and unwind-report paths; obsolete test_restore seam removed in favor of finish() called directly under an injected restore that actually restores CWD then returns the synthetic error

declared_findings.description: to_string_lossy/from_utf8_lossy across ~30 files
declared_findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 5 for every boundary finding 8 names: integration entry-path execution, the rendered-output harness paths and process output, golden text comparison, MOTH_TEST_THREADS and the module-discovery test helpers' file_name().unwrap_or_default(). The HTML-Wasm harness now resolves its artifacts through __dirname so no workspace path crosses a text boundary at all. Remaining to_string_lossy/from_utf8_lossy uses are failure-report rendering (xtask process output echo, path display), never assertion inputs

declared_findings.description: Tests use >= or > assertions where exact counts are needed
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 4: BuiltArtifactIndex (integration) and BuiltOutputs (build-system tests) replace first-match find_map with unique-path lookup and exactly-one selectors; reachable-dependency test asserts the exact emitted path set plus the lowered dependency body and its call site; JS glue, runtime-module and canvas tests assert exactly-one glue/canvas/runtime artifacts at exact paths and that the page imports the module actually emitted; frontend pipeline tests assert exact function-origin multisets and side-table coverage instead of functions_analyzed >= N; borrow-checker pipeline test asserts statement/terminator fact sets equal the lowered statements/blocks and an exact snapshot count; source-package benchmark warning test asserts an exact warning multiset; HIR local lowering tests assert exact authored locals and exactly one assignment to the authored local

declared_findings.description: Golden comparison accepts directory entries as empty golden files
declared_findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 5: the golden comparison decides the artifact kind before reading content. A Directory or NotBuilt entry is a kind mismatch instead of empty bytes, text goldens require strict UTF-8 (invalid UTF-8 is a HarnessFailed, not a silent rewrite), and binary/wasm goldens compare bytes only. Phase 5 closeout: the expected artifact kind is owned by the authored golden's own extension (GoldenFile.expected_kind), so a cross-kind match is rejected before content is read and identical bytes emitted as a different artifact kind cannot satisfy the golden. Regressions cover directory-vs-empty-file, an unbuilt path, invalid UTF-8, binary byte comparison, a duplicate-path artifact set, a JS golden against generic bytes, a wasm golden against generic bytes, an HTML golden produced as JavaScript outside the universal index.html baseline path, and a binary golden that must still match generic bytes

declared_findings.description: HTML/Wasm baseline tests rely on broad fragment matching
declared_findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 5: the HTML shell contract is now ordered, bounded and unique (html_shell_violation, one owner shared with the HTML builder's own shell tests), and the HTML-Wasm baseline derives its required exports from the emitted page.js (instance.exports.<name>) and checks each against the module's typed export kind, with an explicit ABI floor including moth_start. Duplicate exports and imports are rejected, and the page script include must appear exactly once inside the body. Phase 5 closeout: the shell contract is structural rather than a raw substring count. Script and style content is opaque payload the shell inserts, so marker-like text such as a JavaScript string spelling '</body>' no longer counts as a second element, while a marker repeated in real markup is still rejected

declared_findings.description: Node runtime harness tests can hang without timeout
declared_findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 5: the harness owns a tempfile workspace whose removal failure is reported, runs Node under a 30s deadline with kill-and-reap, drains stdout/stderr on their own threads with a 4 MiB bound, decodes protocol output strictly, and parses only supported <script> shapes. Typed RenderHarnessError{kind,message} separates Artifact/Workspace/Spawn/Timeout/ExitStatus/OutputDecoding/OutputProtocol/ScriptShape/Cleanup. Phase 5 closeout: both capture threads are joined before any result is inspected so no failure path drops a live thread; termination always attempts the reap and reports the kill and wait outcomes separately; type="module" is rejected rather than executed under classic semantics because the harness materializes no glue, provider or runtime module and no import map; nameless or malformed attribute tokens fail closed instead of being skipped; and every failure class now has a focused self-test, including Artifact (missing and wrong-kind), Workspace (write collision) and Spawn (a nonexistent interpreter through the process owner's executable seam, not a PATH mutation)

declared_findings.description: Fixture discovery used is_dir/is_file which fail open; non-UTF-8 identities silently skipped
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: symlink_metadata with NotFound-only continue; non-UTF-8 names return error; manifest_path and expect_path checks use symlink_metadata

declared_findings.description: Timing/concurrency tests depend on machine speed
declared_findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 6: the collector drain seam is a condition variable with a bounded deadline used only as deadlock protection, and its waits report the observed state; wait_for_timing_flag's 1,000,000-iteration yield loop is deleted, the dev-server SSE and partial-request tests own and join their server threads, and the SSE registration wait is a bounded deadline that names the observed client count

declared_findings.description: Feature-gated test modules need explicit execution lane mapping
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: eight package-scoped lanes in xtask feature_matrix, run by `just test-feature-matrix`, cover every declared feature. `just feature-lane-check` (part of `just validate`) reads Cargo.toml and every cfg attribute in src and xtask/src, and fails when a declared feature has no lane, when a lane names an undeclared feature, or when a cfg names a feature that does not exist; it writes target/test-reports/feature_lane_coverage.json. The check also exposed that the previous workspace-wide feature commands never ran the default configuration, because xtask depends on moth with features = ["timers"] and Cargo unifies features across one resolve graph

declared_findings.description: Tests rely on filesystem timestamps
declared_findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 6: write_project_outputs returns a typed OutputWriteSummary and the two skip-unchanged tests assert Written / SkippedUnchanged directly, so both 30ms sleeps and both modification-time comparisons are gone; the remaining timestamp reads are the dev-server watch fingerprints, whose tests set modification times explicitly

declared_findings.description: The counters-only feature configuration compiles a test helper no caller can reach
declared_findings.disposition: found in Phase 8 when the counters lane became an executed command; routed to Phase 11. frontend_counters::capture_frontend_counters_for_test, FrontendCounterTestCaptureGuard and the re-export are gated on benchmark_counters, while every caller is gated on all(timers, benchmark_counters), so the counters-only lane emits three dead-code warnings. Nothing fails. It was invisible because `just ci-clippy-native` lints with --all-features and never builds that configuration. The correction is a cfg gate, not a behaviour change, so it is left outside the Patch A evidence boundary

declared_findings.description: CI steps are monolithic
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: the validation workflow runs nine gates (clippy, unit-tests, feature-matrix, integration, docs, benchmarks, timers-erasure, source-audit, honesty-audit) as independent jobs on Linux, macOS and Windows with fail-fast disabled, so one failed family never stops another from reporting. Windows stays non-blocking through a job-level continue-on-error, and validation.mtf > Platform policy now states the two conditions that end that status. The integration, feature-matrix and honesty-audit gates upload target/test-reports/ whether they passed or failed. `just validate` keeps the fail-fast local ordering, and the release workflow deliberately keeps it too. validation.mtf also lost its claim that `just ci-clippy` lints Linux and Windows x64 targets: that recipe does not exist and never did the cross-target work

declared_findings.description: Acceptance-only smoke cases overclaim coverage
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 7: all 12 acceptance-only backend blocks (exactly the 12 smoke-role cases) promoted to rendered_output_exact runtime contracts with a manifest contract and a non-smoke role, and each fixture comment rewritten to state what the case proves; the suite now declares zero acceptance-only blocks and zero smoke roles. Acceptance-only and the smoke role remain legal; schema 7 of the suite inventory reports smoke_role_cases and per-backend weak_contract_reviews so a returning weak contract stays findable

declared_findings.description: Any #[ignore] tests would lack governance
declared_findings.disposition: confirmed: 0 #[ignore] attributes in src or xtask

declared_findings.description: Tests comparing source text create false confidence
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: xtask source_audit is now the one owner of broad-source architecture bans. It walks src and xtask/src once, fails closed on unreadable paths, reports typed findings (timer-erasure, removed-legacy-conversion-name, removed-legacy-payload-variant, unreadable-source) and writes target/test-reports/source_audit.json. Three source-text tests were deleted into it: the diagnostics conversion-name tripwire, old_error_payload_has_been_removed_from_diagnostic_payloads (which read one file) and timer_facade_sources_never_use_cfg_timer_macro (which read four). The audit applies both removed-name bans across the whole tree rather than to the single file each test read. timers-erasure-check kept only its compiled-artifact half and now defines the timer rules that source_audit applies, so no second walk exists to skip a file silently. The remaining include_str! uses in src are CSS and JS assets that a test then parses or executes, which is input, not a source-text assertion

declared_findings.description: Machine-readable reports can become stale or partial
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 8: every report is written to a sibling temporary file, flushed and renamed into place, and a failed write removes the temporary file so the previous report survives instead of a partial new one. Each report carries a RunIdentity (run id, command, host OS and architecture, the features the binary was built with, runner thread count and completion state), and the inventory and triage reports are replaced by a completed:false report before the work starts, so an interrupted run leaves a report that says it did not finish. repository_commit became a typed repository_revision that distinguishes a discovered commit, a run outside a repository, and a failed discovery with its reason, instead of collapsing all three into null. Suite inventory schema 7 to 8; the triage report gained a schema version. Self-tests cover the started/completed transition observed from inside execution, the absence of a partial sibling, a blocked write leaving the previous report intact, and each revision classification

declared_findings.description: xtask bench_history tests manually save/set/restore RAYON_NUM_THREADS without panic-safe guard
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: ScopedEnvVar guard restores on drop including during unwinding

declared_findings.description: Timing tests discarded thread join results
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: surface_thread_panic helper replaces discarded joins

declared_findings.description: assert_diagnostic_reason used manual payload_variant_name mapping instead of reason_key
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: uses diagnostic.identity().reason_key with unwrap_or fallback

declared_findings.description: Test fixtures created CaseExecutionResult with impossible states (passed=true with build_result=None, failure with no build_result or messages)
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: all synthetic CaseExecutionResult fixtures now carry valid build_result or messages; triage test uses valid messages; terse_reporting uses valid BuildResult and CompilerMessages

declared_findings.description: assert_exact_infrastructure_error only checked infrastructure error count, not total error count
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: now requires exactly one error diagnostic overall, and that error must be the expected infrastructure type

declared_findings.description: Integration fixture/expectation loading and runner harness failures travelled as String, forcing negative self-tests to match error identity by prose substrings (fragile; could match the fixture path)
declared_findings.disposition: fixed: added FixtureLoadError{kind,message} (Filesystem/Manifest/ExpectationParse/ExpectationContract/FixtureContract/PathBoundary) across fixture.rs, expectations.rs, manifest.rs and golden discovery; added TestRunnerError with Options/SuitePolicy/InventoryReport/TriageReport/Selection/ThreadPool/Fixture kinds across run_all_test_cases/run_loaded_suite/options.validate/report persistence/selection/thread-pool/env parsing; migrated all negative self-tests in runner.rs, manifest.rs, expectations.rs, fixture.rs to assert error.kind while retaining message prose checks; CLI reads error.message for display

declared_findings.description: find_output_file returned the first matching artifact and collect_built_artifact_paths accepted duplicate normalized paths, so every later assertion inspected one artifact of an ambiguous set
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in Phase 4: BuiltArtifactIndex is built once in validate_success_result before any success assertion and consumed by the HTML/HTML-Wasm baselines, artifact assertions, absence checks, goldens and rendered-output harnesses; validity and collision identity come from the canonical output_path_identity used by the output writer, so the harness rejects exactly the destinations production rejects and folds ASCII case only; an ambiguous or invalid set fails the case as FailureKind::HarnessFailed; self-tests match the typed ArtifactIndexError variants (with one separate test owning the rendered wording) and cover duplicates, ASCII case aliases, non-ASCII case distinctness, parent segments, reserved device basenames, separator normalization, NotBuilt entries and non-UTF-8 paths

declared_findings.description: unused_temp_path promised a nonexistent path without proving it; PID reuse after an interrupted run could return a stale node
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in the pre-Phase-4 review pass: the helper verifies absence with symlink_metadata before returning

declared_findings.description: Helper self-tests and timers conflict tests asserted only catch_unwind(...).is_err(), so an unrelated panic satisfied them
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in the pre-Phase-4 review pass: assert_panics_with requires the panic payload to contain the intended message; migrated test_fs, test_diagnostics, timers conflict tests and the new BuiltOutputs self-tests

declared_findings.description: Phase 1's absence migration covered only the compiler crate; 14 negative Path::exists assertions remained in xtask tests
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in the pre-Phase-4 review pass: added xtask/src/test_fs.rs (assert_path_missing/assert_regular_file/assert_directory with a dangling-symlink regression) and migrated bench_history and benchmark_workspace call sites

declared_findings.description: Build-system glue selectors matched path.contains("_moth/js/glue/"), so a glue module emitted under an unexpected parent directory satisfied an assertion about the glue directory
declared_findings.disposition: fixed in the Phase 4 closeout: glue predicates use a shared GLUE_MODULE_PREFIX with starts_with, matching the already-anchored provider, canvas and runtime selectors, with a self-test proving a nested vendor/_moth/js/glue path does not match

declared_findings.description: frontend_benchmark_rejects_a_busy_raw_session_before_compilation failed once during Phase 5 validation and did not reproduce in 24 subsequent full-suite runs (including 6 at --test-threads=16)
declared_findings.disposition: resolved in Phase 6: the flake reproduced on the Phase 6 baseline run and was the test's evidence, not the compiler. The outer-session 'every aggregate has zero samples' proxy is replaced by two deterministic ordering tests — a missing entry path must fail as TimingSession rather than PathValidation, and invalid source must fail as TimingSession rather than Compilation — neither of which depends on the process-global collector being quiet. The collector stays process-global because cross-thread recording is its production contract

suite_weak_contract_reviews.rationale: A case whose every backend claims only that compilation succeeded is legal when its role says so. Phase 7 promoted every acceptance-only block whose behaviour was observable and renamed the cases that overclaimed, so what this counts is smoke that admits to being smoke.

A block that makes warnings non-contractual accepts every future warning on that case. Phase 7 replaced all four with forbid or exact warning sets; the counter stays so a returning one is a number a reviewer sees rather than a silent weakening.

A failure block matching diagnostics by containment accepts diagnostics beyond the authored multiset. Phase 7 re-measured every one under exact matching and left none; the counter stays because a stale authored reason keeps the weaker contract alive.
Phase 7 promoted all 12 acceptance-only blocks to observable contracts. The counter is the gate on that staying true.
